facts.statement: Squalicorax is an extinct genus of lamniform shark commonly called the crow shark that lived during the Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Squalicorax, commonly known as the crow shark, is a genus of extinct lamniform shark known to have lived during the Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The genus Squalicorax had a global distribution during the Late Cretaceous epoch.
facts.quote: The genus had a global distribution in the Late Cretaceous epoch.

facts.statement: The name Squalicorax comes from the Latin word for shark and the Greek word for raven.
facts.quote: The name Squalicorax is derived from the Latin squalus for shark and the Greek κόραξ, "korax" for raven.

facts.statement: Squalicorax was a medium-sized shark typically measuring between 1.8 and 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Squalicorax was a medium-sized shark, typically measuring about 1.8 - 3 m long.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of Squalicorax pristodontus measured up to 4.8 meters long.
facts.quote: The largest specimen of S. pristodontus, SDSM 47683, was significantly larger, measuring up to 4.8 m long.

facts.statement: Squalicorax had a body shape similar to modern gray reef sharks but possessed teeth strikingly similar to those of a tiger shark.
facts.quote: Their bodies were similar to the modern gray reef sharks, but the shape of the teeth is strikingly similar to that of a tiger shark.

facts.statement: Squalicorax teeth were numerous, relatively small, curved, serrated, and up to 2.5 to 3 centimeters in height.
facts.quote: The teeth are numerous, relatively small, with a curved crown and serrated, up to 2.5 – 3 cm in height.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows Squalicorax was both a coastal predator and scavenger, including a tooth found embedded in the foot bone of a terrestrial hadrosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Squalicorax was a coastal predator and scavenger, as evidenced by a Squalicorax tooth found embedded in the metatarsal (foot) bone of a terrestrial hadrosaurid dinosaur that most likely died on land and ended up in the water.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Squalicorax actively snatched Pteranodon from the air, attacked them while diving, or simply scavenged their remains based on tooth marks found on their bones.
facts.quote: Tooth marks from this shark have also been found on the bones of Pteranodon, but whether the shark actively snatched such large pterosaurs out of the air, attacked them as they dove after prey, or were simply scavenging is not known.

facts.statement: The family Anacoracidae was established by H. Cappetta in 1987.
facts.quote: H. Cappetta, Handbook of Paleoichthyology (Gustav Fischer, 1987)

facts.statement: Squalicorax belongs to the family Anacoracidae, an authority established by Cappetta in 1987.
The world's largest and most complete semi-articulated Squalicorax fossil, measuring over 3 meters, was discovered in 2014 in Morden, Manitoba, Canada.
facts.quote: The world's largest and most complete semi-articulated fossil of Squalicorax was found in 2014 in stores of the Canadian Fossil Discovery Centre in Morden, Manitoba, in Canada, where it is now displayed. It measures more than 3 m in length.

facts.statement: Squalicorax volgensis is the oldest species of the genus, originating from the Early Cretaceous of the Volga region and described by L. Glickman et al. in 1971.
facts.quote: Squalicorax volgensis - the oldest species of the genus, from the Early Cretaceous of the Volga – was described by L. Glickman et al. in 1971.

facts.statement: Squalicorax pristodontus is the largest species in the genus, with estimates based on tooth size suggesting it grew to 4.8 meters in length.
facts.quote: Squalicorax pristodontus (Agassiz, 1843) is the largest species, exceeding 3 m in length. From the size of its largest known teeth, it can be estimated that S. pristodontus grew to 4.8 m in length.

facts.statement: Squalicorax had a typical shark shape and could measure up to 5 meters, averaging around 2 meters.
facts.quote: Como Cretoxyrhina es un miembro extinto de los Lamniformes. Tenía la forma típica de un tiburón, medía hasta 5 metros (promediando los 2 metros).

facts.statement: The body shape and structure of the placoid scales indicate that Squalicorax was capable of swimming quickly.
facts.quote: La forma del cuerpo y la estructura de las escamas placoideas truncas indican la habilidad de nadar rápidamente.

facts.statement: The genus Squalicorax existed from the Callovian to the Danian, spanning from 165.3 to 61.66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Danian (165.3 to 61.66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Squalicorax is one of only three Cretaceous lamniform sharks known to have serrated teeth, alongside Pseudocorax and Galeocorax.
facts.quote: Squalicorax is one of three Cretaceous lamniformes to garner serrations along with Pseudocorax and Galeocorax.

rejected.quote: Other food sources included sea turtles, mosasaurs, ichthyodectid fish, and other marine life.
